conviction_note: Nothing decisive and unpriced turned up. The filed items are small and point both ways: a seasonal Q3 revenue pull inside the guide, against a quantified Catalyst savings figure promised for this call, director/activist buying, shorts covering 43% into late September, an earlier-than-usual report date and a stock trading below net cash. They net to +0.9 points, so p_up sits at 52. abs_move_pct is 12, not the 3.3 median, because the last two prints moved +22% and +34% on the guidance line, coverage is one analyst, turnover is about $1.3m a day, and three transitions (rebrand, new coach compensation plan, new product line) all land in this quarter.
bar: Company Q3 2026 guide: revenue $60-80m (midpoint $70m), loss per share $0.15-0.65 (midpoint -$0.40), excluding one-time Catalyst costs (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051845/medq22026earningsrelease.htm). The street estimates disagree: ChartMill -$0.35 / $72.0m (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/MED/estimates, via search snippet; the page returned 403); the Earnings Whispers page -$0.60 / $69.18m, likely stale from before the guide (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/MED); an Earnings Whispers snippet -$0.40 / $62.45m; MarketBeat's pre-guide figure -$0.62 / $68m (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/medifast-nysemed-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-03/). I sized against the company guide midpoint. Because the estimates disagree, findings that depend on the bar are kept small.
positioning_check: Short interest is falling. Per Equibles' FINRA settlements: 1,639,608 shares (2026-07-15), 1,484,483 (07-31), 1,824,259 (08-14, 7.4 days to cover), 1,882,921 (08-31, 15.1 dtc), 1,862,070 (09-15, 20.0 dtc), then 1,053,225 on 2026-09-30 (7.3 dtc, about 9.4% of 11.18m shares outstanding) (https://equibles.com/stocks/med/shortinterest). The 10-15 settlement publishes 10-26, the print day. No usable skew: the option chain is unusable (ATM spread 86% of mid, skew null; ATM IV 58.6% on the 11-20 expiry; put/call OI 0.24, call-heavy). Run-up: -3.1% over 20 days, -0.8% over 5. Spot $11.79, 10% off the 52-week high, 25% above the low. Steamboat Capital (director Parsa Kiai) holds about 7%+ and bought in August.

findings.finding: Q3 has been Medifast's seasonally weakest quarter: revenue fell 15.3% Q2-to-Q3 in 2025 ($105.6m to $89.4m) and 16.8% in 2024 ($168.6m to $140.2m). Active earning coaches fell 16% Q1-to-Q2 2026 (14,000 to 11,700) and management expects further declines. A repeat of the seasonal pattern on Q2's $76.4m gives about $65m, below the $70m guide midpoint but inside the $60-80m range. Against that, 2026 broke seasonality once already: Q2 was flat on Q1 ($76.4m vs $76.0m) because revenue per coach rose about 20% q/q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue of $76.4m beat roughly $72.7m consensus, together with a large EPS beat and a raised FY EPS guide; the stock rose +34.3% (baseline). Q1 2026's revenue beat came with +22.5%. The name has paid for beats recently, but on EPS and guidance rather than on revenue alone.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide range is $20m wide and the street estimates scatter from $62m to $72m, so nobody holds a precise bar. A seasonal read below the midpoint is inside the guide. If it were priced, consensus would sit near $65m, not $69-72m.
findings.independence: The 2026 coach counts and Q2 revenue come from the Q2 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051845/medq22026earningsrelease.htm); Q1 2026 from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026029812/medq12026earningsrelease.htm. This is inference from company history, not a Q3 datapoint.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CFO said Catalyst savings could not yet be quantified ('millions of dollars of savings') and that full detail would come on the Q3 call. Management targets a return to profitability in Q4 2026. The first quantified savings figure and the Q4 path therefore land on this print. Stephens (James Salera), the only analyst on the call, asked about the savings and got no number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 FY EPS guide raise (from -$1.55/-$2.75 to -$0.25/-$1.75) drove the +34.3% reaction (baseline; https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/med/news/earnings/medifast-nysemed-beats-expectations-in-strong-q2-cy2026-stock-jumps-128percent). This stock moves hard on the guidance line.
findings.why_not_priced: No dollar figure exists in the public record, and with one analyst no estimate of savings is in consensus EPS. The stock has gone flat at about $12 since August rather than drifting up, which it would have done if a large savings number were expected.
findings.independence: The Q2 release confirms Catalyst's purpose (facility rationalization, AI efficiencies) and the Havre de Grace lease cut (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051845/medq22026earningsrelease.htm). The 10-Q records a $12.5m right-of-use remeasurement on the reduced-footprint lease (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910329/000162828026051928/med-20260630.htm). Both are company documents.

findings.finding: Director Parsa Kiai (Steamboat Capital, a 13D filer at 7.1% as of 2026-08-21) bought about 120k shares in the open market at $11.60-12.26, after the Q2 jump: 29.3k and 43.2k shares on 08-19/20, 4.3k on 08-24 and 43.2k on 08-26. Holdings are about 727k shares through the two funds.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since August and the stock has not moved, so it is largely priced. It is filed because a board member buying after a 34% move, ahead of a quarter he has visibility into, is a modest information signal.
findings.independence: 13D/A: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910329/000121390026092590/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml ; later Form 4s: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910329/000121390026094862/xslF345X06/ownership.xml (same filer, so not independent).

findings.finding: Director and former CEO Daniel Chard sold 19,089 shares through a family trust on 2026-09-28/29 at $11.73-11.98 under a Rule 10b5-1 plan. He retains about 336k shares directly and indirectly.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small, under a pre-arranged plan, and made by a departed CEO whose filing address is now Nu Skin. It carries little information; it is filed only for completeness.

findings.finding: Short interest fell 43% in the second half of September, from 1,862,070 shares (09-15, 20 days to cover) to 1,053,225 (09-30, 7.3 days to cover, about 9.4% of shares). About 800k shares were covered, roughly 8 days of average volume, ahead of an earlier-than-usual print.
findings.why_not_priced: The figure is published but rarely read on a $130m name. The cut runs both ways. Fewer shorts means less squeeze fuel, which argues for a smaller upside tail than the 20%-short setup the sweep described. It also means shorts no longer press for a downside print.
findings.independence: The sweep's 08-14 figure (1.8m, 7.4 dtc, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/med/short-interest/) matches Equibles' series; the 09-30 figure has one source only.

findings.finding: Medifast moved the Q3 report earlier and switched session: results come Monday 2026-10-26 before the open, against the Q3 2025 report on 2025-11-03 and the amc Q2 2026 report on 2026-08-03. An earlier date than the prior-year cadence is weakly associated with better news.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (relay of the company's announcement; exact day not readable, the page returns 403)
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators still list 11-03 or 11-05 (Earnings Whispers) as the report date, so the schedule change itself is not widely registered. It is a weak proxy at best.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 date: https://businesswire.com/news/home/20251103877853/en/Medifast-Announces-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results ; this is a proxy, not company data.

findings.finding: Cash and investments were $169.8m with no debt at 2026-06-30, against a market cap of about $132m (11.18m shares at $11.79). Working capital is guided above $145m at year-end, so the stock trades below net cash. That limits the downside on a weak operating print unless Catalyst one-time costs prove large.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (-0.8%) and Q3 2025 (+0.8%) were damped reactions with the stock near net cash (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and largely priced. 'Cheap' is not an edge. It is filed small only because it shapes the asymmetry of the reaction, and Catalyst cash costs that are not yet quantified could erode it.
findings.independence: Q2 release, same numbers (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051845/medq22026earningsrelease.htm); not independent.

findings.finding: The GLP-1 headwind intensified through 2026. Lilly's oral orforglipron (Foundayo) launched with $149-349 a month cash pricing; Truveta counted 5,723 patients from 04-01 to 07-06, 40% new to GLP-1s. Novo's oral Wegovy has passed 600k US prescriptions. Medifast itself names 'rapid adoption of GLP-1 medications' as the cause of its coach decline.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the company guided with this headwind in view. This is macro-to-company transmission with no Q3-specific datapoint, so it is filed small.
findings.independence: Company attribution in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051845/medq22026earningsrelease.htm); this is a proxy.

findings.finding: Three transitions land inside Q3 2026, per the 10-Q: the OPTAVIA brand was replaced by Trilivy (07-17), a new coach compensation plan launched in Q3, and the Reset Fueling product line was rolled out ('fully to market this quarter'). Obsolete-inventory allowance fell from $4.3m to $3.3m in H1 with no explanation. A new product line can pull orders forward, while a comp-plan change in a coach network can disrupt it. I found no public data on coach or client reception.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is unknown. No coach forum, app or review data surfaced on Trilivy, so nobody outside has a read. This raises the variance (abs_move_pct) rather than carrying a sign.
findings.independence: The Trilivy launch release (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260717813453/en/Medifast-Enters-a-New-Era-Introducing-Trilivy-a-Science-Backed-Metabolic-Health-System) says the same.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (unusable chain), and the 20-day run-up is mildly negative (-3.1%). The slight positive lean from insiders, short covering and the savings reveal cuts mildly against the drift, so p_up is held at 52.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): the seasonal Q3 revenue finding lands inside the $60-80m guided range and the street bar is disputed, so it moved from -0.5 to -0.3.
Rule 8 (thin coverage) plus rule 1 (this name pays on the guidance line, +22% and +34% on the last two prints): abs_move_pct moved from 10 to 12.
The 'cheap is not a finding' guidance cut the net-cash finding from +0.3 to +0.2, kept small rather than dropped under the core's filing rule.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest had already been checked; it argues against a large squeeze tail and left the signs unchanged.
Nothing else changed. The other sizes and p_up 52 stand.
